correctness.rationale: Exact bridge Kirchhoff summation yields path increments u(j)-u(j-1)=sum_{k>=j}f(k) and the head equation L_H v=f_H-F e_o. The zero-vertex-mean condition yields the coefficient b_k=[mk+k(k-1)/2]/N and the tip identity. Spectral projection on the orthogonal complement of head constants gives |v(o)|<=(sqrt(m)+m)/gamma; hence a uniform finite-norm deviation. The zero-mean bounded-cube support function equals the ℓ1 distance from a constant, by finite-dimensional convex duality. The normalized coefficients differ by at most 1/(2N) from a uniformly 1-Lipschitz quadratic, making the Riemann-sum error at most 1/N. The minimizer of the continuum absolute-deviation objective is the median of an atom plus a strictly increasing quadratic pushforward. The two median regimes integrate to a continuously differentiable piecewise cubic with distinct second derivatives at one half. For a clique, L_H=mI-J gives its exact coefficient list and median norm; the two path-scaled limits are 1/8 and 1/2. The packaged checker reconstructed full rational pseudoinverses and passed 2271 comparisons; it is corroborative only.

value.rationale: The sharp pendant response is a natural finite-network stability invariant for balanced bounded loads. The new result is not just a single graph matrix computation: every uniformly gapped head has the same quantitative continuum profile, with a sharp source-pattern switch at half mass and a jump in second derivative. A full finite clique median formula and a macroscopic factor-four contrast supply interpretable endpoints and reproducibility. The conclusion identifies which macrogeometry, rather than head microstructure, controls worst-case tip voltage. There is no claimed global endpoint matrix norm or journal-sized result.
